backlogged.summary: In lib/run.mjs `finish`, resolveItems runs before setStatus. If the features.json write then fails, the backlog items are already marked resolved_by while the feature is not passed. Ordering it after the status write, or making it retryable, would remove the window.
recordEntries bumps `seen` once per entry. Two entries in the same round that carry the same backlog_id raise seen by 2 but add only one `sources` tag, so seen and sources.length can drift apart.

An existing item that a later entry hits does not get its priority updated or raised, even when the new entry carries a higher severity. This follows the contract (no retroactive priority), but the evaluator's higher severity is silently lost.

Items without an id get B<n> only in memory when status or the prompt reads them, and are persisted on the next core write. This is consistent and tested. Until that write happens, the id shown in status is not stored anywhere.

lint-contract now reads backlog.json for every run. A corrupt or duplicate-id backlog therefore makes lint-contract exit 2 for contracts that do not use resolves. SPEC §7.7 documents this, but it is broader than the AC-6 wording.
